title: SSRF via Tainted Outbound URL Requests
pattern: Passing raw client-provided string URLs directly to outbound HTTP client request sinks or redirection endpoints without validation.
why_bad: Exposes the server to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Open Redirection. An attacker can supply internal network targets (e.g. `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data`) to exfiltrate database keys or private metadata.
detection: Outbound request library invocations (like `get`, `post`, `fetch`) receiving raw input strings from requests without domain-level assertion check.
fix: Parse input strings into typed `Url` objects, enforce the `https` scheme, and strictly validate the destination domain against an explicit allowlist before execution.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 6, p. 113.
